key_insight: Routing supervision by teacher agreement (EWAD) combined with a geometric capacity-preserving constraint (CPDP) lets a student model selectively learn from multiple heterogeneous teachers, improving reliability for low-resource abstractive summarization.
problem_solved: Low-resource abstractive summarization suffers from limited labeled data and noisy or conflicting signals from multiple teacher models. This work addresses how to distill multi-teacher supervision reliably so a compact student learns useful, consistent behavior rather than inheriting teacher disagreement.
method: EWAD (Entropy Weighted Agreement Aware Distillation): token-level routing that weights teacher vs. gold supervision based on inter-teacher agreement/entropy.
CPDP (Capacity Proportional Divergence Preservation): geometric constraint that positions the student relative to heterogeneous teachers to preserve useful divergences proportional to capacity.
Integrated multi-teacher distillation pipeline that combines agreement-aware supervision routing with capacity-aware student positioning, evaluated on Bangla summarization datasets.
impact: Provides a practical, reliability-aware recipe for multi-teacher distillation that helps practitioners train smaller, more robust abstractive summarizers in low-resource languages or domains where teacher signals conflict or are noisy.
visual_elements: Flow diagram of training pipeline showing student, multiple teachers, EWAD token-level routing, and gold reference routing.
Illustration of CPDP: geometric plot with teacher embeddings and constrained student position relative to them.
Bar chart or table comparing model performance/robustness across the evaluated Bangla datasets (teacher-only vs. EWAD+CPDP student).
Icon set: 'agreement' (people/teachers converging), 'entropy' gauge, and 'compact model' (small model icon) to summarize benefits.
paper_title: Reliability Gated Multi-Teacher Distillation for Low Resource Abstractive Summarization
paper_authors: Dipto Sumit, Ankan Kumar Roy, Sadia Khair Rodela, Atia Haque Asha, Mourchona Afrin
